outcomeTiers.explanation: You helped where it mattered and held your ground where it counted — and said the honest thing out loud instead of just feeling it.
You got through it without either of you really losing, though something between you still needs a real conversation eventually.
You avoided the hard part. The pattern's still there, just a little further under the surface now.
You walked back the one honest thing you'd said the moment it got uncomfortable — which is usually how patterns like this stay exactly the same.

start.message: Sam's been your friend since school — the kind of friendship where you've never really needed to explain yourself, the one who'd drop everything if you actually needed them. A few days before any of this, Sam bails on plans with you last-minute — again — mumbling something about "just a lot going on right now." You don't think much of it at the time.

data.location: A text thread, a few days earlier

choices.label: No worries, we'll reschedule.
That's the third time, but okay.

reasons.savvy: You noticed the pattern before anyone forced you to.

the_call.message: "Please tell me you're free right now," Sam says before you've even said hello. "My car just died on the ring road, I've got nowhere else to turn. Can you come get me?"

choices.label: Yeah. Where are you?

reasons.integrity: You showed up without making Sam ask twice.
reasons.streetSmarts: You didn't weigh what this costs you before saying yes.

choices.label: I can come, but I need to leave by 6:30.

reasons.savvy: You said yes without pretending your own plans don't exist.
reasons.streetSmarts: Naming your limit up front protects both of you.

choices.label: How are you getting home if I can't?

reasons.streetSmarts: You problem-solved instead of absorbing the whole thing yourself.
reasons.savvy: Asking the question shifts the frame from 'rescue me' to 'let's figure this out.'

choices.label: Sam... you know this is the third time, right?

reasons.savvy: You said the thing you'd been noticing instead of swallowing it again.
reasons.integrity: Naming a pattern honestly, even when it's uncomfortable, is its own kind of loyalty.

sam_reacts_yes.message: "Oh thank God. I'm on the ring road, just past the Texaco." You grab your keys and go. Sam's already smiling when you pull up — relieved, grateful, and completely unaware that you just walked out of something that mattered to you.

choices.label: "That was a bit of a scramble for me, by the way."

reasons.integrity: You said it instead of quietly banking the resentment.

choices.label: Say nothing. Drive.

reasons.streetSmarts: Letting it go quietly doesn't make it not cost you — it just makes the cost invisible.

sam_reacts_limit.message: "Yeah — yeah, of course. Thanks." There's a tiny pause before the thanks. Not rude. Just... the fraction of a second where Sam was expecting unconditional and got something slightly less. You show up. Sam's in the car by 6:28. Nobody mentions the deadline.

choices.label: "Are we good? You went quiet for a second there."

reasons.savvy: You caught the micro-shift in Sam's tone and named it instead of letting it fester.

choices.label: Drop Sam off. Head to your thing.

reasons.streetSmarts: You set a boundary, kept it, and moved on.

sam_reacts_solve.message: "I... don't really have another option? That's why I'm calling you." There's a wobble in Sam's voice you weren't expecting. Not anger. Something closer to embarrassment.

choices.label: Okay — I'll come. Just tell me where you are.

reasons.savvy: You heard the wobble and adjusted.
reasons.integrity: Pivoting from problem-solving to showing up when someone's clearly struggling.

choices.label: What about a taxi? I can send you the money.

reasons.streetSmarts: You found a way to help without absorbing the whole problem yourself.

sam_reacts_confront.message: Silence. Five full seconds of it. Then, quietly: "Yeah. I know." Another pause. "I didn't think you were counting."

choices.label: I'm not counting. I'm just... noticing. Where are you? I'm coming.

reasons.savvy: You named the pattern and then still showed up — that's the strongest version of this move.
reasons.streetSmarts: Confronting AND helping is harder than picking one.
reasons.integrity: You separated the boundary from the rescue instead of making Sam choose between hearing the truth and getting help.

choices.label: I'm not trying to be harsh. But I need you to hear it.

reasons.integrity: You held the honest thing even when Sam's silence made it uncomfortable.
reasons.streetSmarts: The timing — mid-crisis, on the phone — isn't ideal for this conversation.

choices.label: Sorry — forget I said that. Where are you?

reasons.savvy: Walking it back erased the one moment that might have changed something.
reasons.integrity: Apologising for a boundary you meant undoes the honesty it took to set it.

sam_hears_it.message: Sam looks at you differently for a second. "I didn't realise it actually bothered you. I guess I've just gotten used to you being the one who shows up." It's not quite an apology, but it's not nothing either.

data.location: Sam's place, a few days later

choices.label: I don't mind helping. I mind being the only option.

reasons.integrity: You named the real issue instead of the surface complaint.
reasons.savvy: You separated 'helping' from 'being the default' — that's the actual distinction.

choices.label: Honestly, don't worry about it.

reasons.integrity: Waving it off protected the moment and cost you the pattern actually changing.

sam_hears_it_after.message: Sam goes quiet for a second. "Yeah. I think I've been doing that." They look embarrassed, but they don't try to argue with you. "I'm sorry."

data.location: Sam's place, a few days later

choices.label: "I appreciate you saying that."

reasons.integrity: You accepted the apology without pretending the pattern never happened.

choices.label: "It's fine. I just don't want it to get weird between us."

reasons.streetSmarts: You kept the relationship bigger than the argument.

sam_hears_it_later.message: Three weeks later, your phone buzzes. Sam: "Hey — can I ask before I assume you'll help this time?" You smile. It's a small message, but you know exactly why it matters.

choices.label: Reply.
choices.consequence: The friendship doesn't become perfect. But something has shifted: Sam asks, you answer honestly, and neither of you has to guess what the other means anymore.

sam_hears_it_avoided.message: Sam smiles and lets the subject drop. You do too. For the rest of the evening, everything feels normal — almost suspiciously normal.

choices.label: Let the moment pass.

reasons.streetSmarts: You chose short-term comfort over changing the pattern.

sam_hears_it_avoided_later.message: The following week, Sam texts: "Hey, quick favour?" You stare at the message for a few seconds. It's a small thing. But now you recognise the feeling immediately.

choices.label: "Actually — can we talk about something first?"
choices.consequence: It's awkward, but the conversation finally happens when neither of you is stranded, stressed or defensive. Sam listens. The pattern doesn't disappear overnight, but at least it is no longer invisible.

choices.label: "Sure."
choices.consequence: You do the favour. Neither of you mentions the conversation you almost had. Nothing explodes. That's almost the problem — the pattern survives because it never becomes uncomfortable enough to change.

sam_assumes.message: A week later, Sam texts: "Hey, quick favour — can you pick something up for me on your way home?" It's small. It's casual. It's exactly the shape of the pattern you didn't name.

choices.label: Sure.

reasons.savvy: You're not missing the pattern anymore — you're choosing to absorb it.
reasons.integrity: Saying yes when you mean 'I wish you'd stop asking' isn't generosity.

choices.label: Actually — can we talk about something?

reasons.savvy: Better late than in another three months.
reasons.integrity: Bringing it up now, unprompted, when the stakes are low, is actually the braver version.

sam_assumes_aftermath.message: You pick it up. When you hand it over, Sam barely notices what it took to do it. "You're a lifesaver," they say, already moving on to the next thing.

choices.label: Say nothing.
choices.consequence: You walk away knowing you weren't actually okay with it. The next time Sam asks, you'll have to decide whether to keep absorbing it or finally say something.

sam_assumes_talk.message: Sam takes a long breath. "I genuinely didn't realise I'd been doing that." There's a pause. "I don't want you feeling like you have to say yes to me."

choices.label: "Then I probably need to get better at saying no too."
choices.consequence: Neither of you gets a perfect apology or a dramatic resolution. You just leave the conversation knowing the rules of the friendship are a little clearer now — and that might be enough.

choices.label: "We'll figure it out."
choices.consequence: The conversation ends gently. Nothing is magically fixed, but the next time Sam asks for something, there is a little more room for you to answer honestly.

sam_surprised.message: "Wait — you're still coming?" Sam sounds genuinely surprised. "I thought... after what you just said..." You can hear them recalibrating. This isn't what Sam expected.

choices.label: Yeah, I'm still coming. Saying it and leaving would've been worse.

reasons.integrity: You showed that confrontation and care aren't opposites.
reasons.savvy: The combination of honest words and a physical showing-up is the strongest signal you could have sent.

choices.label: I'm not going to leave you stranded. But we need to talk about this properly.

reasons.streetSmarts: Deferring the hard conversation to a better moment — without dropping it — is the most effective version of this.

sam_surprised_after.message: The rest of the drive is quieter than usual. Sam doesn't apologise again. They don't need to. Two days later, your phone buzzes.

choices.label: Open the message.
choices.consequence: Sam has been thinking about what you said. Nothing is magically fixed, but for the first time the friendship feels like something both of you are responsible for — not something you quietly carry.

sam_surprised_boundary.message: The drive home is quiet. Neither of you pushes it. A few days later, you meet for coffee — without a crisis forcing the conversation.

choices.label: "Okay. Let's actually talk about it."
choices.consequence: The conversation is uncomfortable, but calmer than it would have been on the ring road. You don't solve the whole friendship in one coffee. You do, however, stop pretending there isn't a problem.

new_info.message: A week later, you run into Sam's sister at the shops. She pulls you aside. "Has Sam talked to you? About Mum?" You shake your head. "She was diagnosed last month. Sam's been driving her to appointments three times a week. They haven't told anyone."

choices.label: Call Sam. Right now.

reasons.savvy: You updated your read of the situation the moment you had new information.
reasons.integrity: Reaching out immediately, without needing to process it first, is its own kind of showing up.

choices.label: Sit with it for a while. You need to think.

reasons.streetSmarts: Processing time is valid — but Sam was carrying this alone every day you spent thinking about it.

new_info_call.message: Sam is quiet for a long time. "I didn't know how to tell you," they finally say. "I didn't want everyone looking at me like something was wrong."

choices.label: "You don't have to handle it alone."
choices.consequence: The conversation about the favours suddenly looks different. You weren't wrong to notice the pattern — but now you know there was a whole part of Sam's life you couldn't see. You don't forget the boundary. You just understand it differently.

new_info_late.message: Three days later, you finally call. Sam answers on the second ring. "I figured you'd call eventually," they say. There's no anger in it. Just tiredness.

data.location: Three days later, over the phone

choices.label: "Tell me what you need."
choices.consequence: You help where you can. But you keep thinking about the three days you spent wondering what to do. Sometimes giving someone space is kindness. Sometimes they were hoping you'd close the distance.
